title: Find and install drivers for Halden laptops and desktops
summary: Drivers are published per model on the Halden Support Drivers page and through the Halden Update app.
steps: Open Halden Update (preinstalled) and choose Check for updates; install everything marked Recommended.
Without the app: go to the Drivers page, enter the service tag or choose the model, filter by your OS.
Install chipset first, then graphics, audio, network, touchpad and camera, restarting when asked.
Unknown devices in Device Manager: right-click, Properties, Details, Hardware Ids; search that ID on the Drivers page.
escalate_if: A driver install fails with a hardware error code or the device is missing from Device Manager entirely.

title: Update BIOS / UEFI firmware safely
summary: Firmware updates fix stability and security issues. Interrupting one can leave the device unbootable.
steps: Connect the charger and keep it connected; battery should be above 30%.
Suspend BitLocker or device encryption before updating so you are not asked for the recovery key afterwards.
Run the update from Halden Update, or download the firmware file and run it from Windows.
If Windows will not start, copy the firmware file to a FAT32 USB stick, press F12 at boot and choose Firmware Update.
Do not power off during the update; the device may restart several times. Rollback to the previous version is available from the same F12 menu.
escalate_if: The device does not start after a firmware update.

title: Reset or reinstall the operating system
summary: Halden Recovery restores the factory image from the recovery partition or from a USB stick.
steps: Back up files first; a reset can remove personal data.
From Windows: Settings, System, Recovery, Reset this PC.
If Windows will not start: press F11 at power-on to open Halden Recovery and choose Restore factory image.
No recovery partition: create a USB stick with the Halden Recovery Media tool on another computer (16 GB or larger) and boot from it with F12.
For boot loops or INACCESSIBLE_BOOT_DEVICE, run the built-in disk check from the F12 diagnostics menu before reinstalling.
escalate_if: Diagnostics report a disk failure, or the customer reports missing or unreadable data.

title: Wi-Fi or Bluetooth drops, slow, or missing
summary: Most wireless problems are fixed by updating the wireless driver and changing power settings.
steps: Install the latest wireless and Bluetooth drivers from Halden Update.
Device Manager, network adapter, Power Management: clear 'Allow the computer to turn off this device to save power'.
For 5 GHz networks not showing, set the adapter's Preferred Band to 5 GHz and confirm the router channel is supported.
Forget the network and reconnect; run the Network troubleshooter.
If the wireless option disappeared, run the F12 diagnostics wireless test.

title: Screen flicker, blinking or wrong resolution after an update
summary: Flicker after an update is usually a graphics driver or panel power-saving setting.
steps: Reinstall the graphics driver from Halden Update (not the generic Windows driver).
Turn off Panel Self Refresh and adaptive brightness in the Halden Display app.
Set the refresh rate under Display settings, Advanced display.
Run the F12 built-in LCD self-test: if the flicker appears in the self-test, the panel needs service.
escalate_if: The flicker appears in the built-in LCD self-test.

title: Improve slow performance
summary: Slowness is usually background updates, startup apps, low disk space or a power mode setting.
steps: Let pending updates finish and restart.
Task Manager, Startup apps: disable anything you do not need at startup.
Set the power mode to Balanced or Best performance; check the Halden Power app is not in Quiet mode.
Keep at least 15% of the drive free; run Storage Sense.
Run the F12 diagnostics; a failing drive can cause slowness.
escalate_if: Diagnostics report a drive or memory error.

title: Device will not power on: checks before service
summary: Steps an agent asks for before approving a repair for a device that will not power on.
steps: Laptop: disconnect everything, hold power 30 seconds, connect only the original charger, try again.
Note the charging LED pattern; three amber blinks indicate a battery fault, two indicate the power adapter.
Desktop: try a different outlet and power cable; check the PSU switch.
Monitor: try a different power cable and input, press the self-test button.
escalate_if: Any sign of heat damage, swelling, burning smell or smoke: stop and escalate to Trust & Safety.

title: Cracked or damaged screen
summary: Physical damage is not covered by the standard warranty; it may be covered by Accidental Damage Protection.
steps: Stop using the device if glass fragments are loose.
Back up data through an external monitor if possible.
An agent checks coverage and arranges repair or a quote.
escalate_if: Battery damage is visible or suspected.

title: Keyboard keys or touchpad not working
summary: Check software causes before service.
steps: Restart and test in the F12 diagnostics keyboard test.
If keys work in diagnostics, reinstall the keyboard and touchpad drivers.
If keys fail in diagnostics, an agent arranges a keyboard replacement.
escalate_if: The keyboard or touchpad is being pushed up from below (possible battery swelling).

title: Fan noise and overheating
summary: Check thermals and run the fan test before a part is dispatched.
steps: Use the device on a hard surface; clean vents with compressed air.
Update BIOS and the Halden Power app.
Run the F12 diagnostics fan test and note any error code.
Servers: check the fan status in the management controller.
escalate_if: Smoke, melting, burning smell, or a server fan failure on a production system.

title: Dead and stuck pixel policy
summary: Clarity monitors and Aero laptops are replaced under warranty when pixel defects exceed the policy thresholds.
steps: Run the built-in self-test (monitor: hold the menu button 5 seconds; laptop: F12 LCD test) to confirm the pixel is not on the source.
Policy: replacement for any bright (always-on) pixel, or for 3 or more dark pixels, during the warranty period.
If your device meets the policy, reply with the service tag and a photo, and an agent will arrange the exchange.

title: Dock or external displays not detected
summary: Most Dock D3 problems are fixed by firmware and driver updates.
steps: Update the dock firmware with the Halden Dock Updater, then the laptop BIOS and graphics driver.
Disconnect the dock from power for 30 seconds, then reconnect power before the laptop cable.
Use the USB-C cable supplied with the dock; check the port supports display output.
For two monitors, confirm the laptop supports multi-stream transport in the dock compatibility list.

title: Check warranty status and coverage
summary: Coverage is looked up by service tag.
steps: Provide the service tag (on the bottom label or in the BIOS).
The lookup returns the plan, end date, and whether service is onsite or mail-in.

title: Extend or upgrade coverage
summary: Extensions are quoted by the renewals team.
steps: Provide the service tag(s).
Renewals sends a quote; expired coverage may need an inspection first.

title: Transfer ownership
summary: Warranty follows the device; registration can be changed with proof of purchase or a transfer form.
steps: Complete the ownership transfer form with the service tag.
An agent verifies and updates the registration.

title: Accidental damage coverage
summary: Drops, spills and electrical surges are covered only under Accidental Damage Protection.
steps: Power off a wet device and do not charge it.
An agent checks whether ADP is active and how many claims remain.
escalate_if: Liquid near the battery with heat or smell.

title: Track a replacement part
summary: Part shipments are tracked by order number.
steps: Provide the order number (ORD-########).
The lookup returns carrier, tracking number and estimated delivery.

title: Wrong, damaged or missing part
summary: An agent verifies the part number and reships.
steps: Do not install the part.
Send photos of the part label and packaging.

title: Return a defective part
summary: Defective parts must be returned within 10 days with the prepaid label.
steps: Pack the old part in the replacement's packaging.
An agent issues or reissues the prepaid label.

title: Book or change an onsite technician visit
summary: Approved onsite cases can be booked or moved with the self-scheduling link.
steps: Provide the case number (CS-#######).
Use the scheduling link to pick or change a 4-hour window.
Changes are free until 6 pm the day before the visit.

title: Missed technician visit
summary: A dispatch coordinator investigates and rebooks with priority.
steps: Provide the case number.
The coordinator contacts the field partner and offers the earliest slot.

title: Refund status
summary: Refunds are issued within 5 business days of the return being received; banks take 3 to 10 more days.
steps: Provide the order number.
The lookup returns the return-received date and refund date.

title: Invoice copies
summary: Invoices can be re-sent to the email on the order.
steps: Provide the order number.
Company name or VAT changes need an agent.

title: Duplicate or incorrect charge
summary: Billing reviews the payment record; pending authorizations often drop off in 3 to 5 days.
steps: Provide the order number and the dates and amounts on the statement.

title: Return a product
summary: Products bought direct can be returned within 30 days in original condition.
steps: Provide the order number.
An agent confirms eligibility and issues the return authorization.

title: Enterprise outage: severity 1 intake
summary: Business-wide outages go to the enterprise duty manager immediately; no scripted troubleshooting by email.
steps: Page the duty manager.
Collect the service tags, error logs and contact number.

title: Degraded RAID or failed disk
summary: Degraded arrays risk data loss; a storage specialist owns the case.
steps: Advise not to reboot or replace disks until the specialist reviews the controller log.

title: Data loss
summary: Stop using the drive; a data-recovery specialist owns the case.
steps: Advise the customer to stop using the device to avoid overwriting data.

title: Battery swelling, smoke or burning smell
summary: Safety incident. Trust & Safety contacts the customer the same day.
steps: Tell the customer to stop using and unplug the device, keep it on a non-flammable surface away from people, and not to puncture or press the battery.

title: Security incident or stolen device
summary: Security team owns the case; may involve remote lock and account protection.
steps: Do not ask for passwords. Record the service tag and when the incident happened.

title: Legal or regulatory threat
summary: Customer relations and legal review. No commitments in writing by frontline staff.
steps: Acknowledge receipt only.

title: Personal data requests
summary: Access, deletion and objection requests go to the Privacy Office, which has statutory deadlines.
steps: Acknowledge receipt only; do not change or delete records from the support desk.
